title: Mortara converts first pole into first win at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Edoardo Mortara won the fourth DTM round from pole for Audi Team Rosberg by 1.068 seconds from Martin Tomczyk's BMW, after a chaotic opening lap and a safety car.

chapters.title: Audi looks for a first win in Austria
text: Two weeks after Brands Hatch, the DTM moved to the Red Bull Ring at Spielberg for the fourth of its ten races, on Sunday 3 June. The season so far had been shared between two makes: Mercedes had won twice, through Gary Paffett at Hockenheim and Brands Hatch, and BMW once, through Bruno Spengler at the Lausitzring. Audi had yet to win in 2012, although its drivers had filled five of the top ten places in Britain, with Mike Rockenfeller third behind Paffett and Spengler.

Paffett arrived as the clear points leader on 68, ahead of Spengler on 43, Mattias Ekström on 35, Jamie Green on 34 and Rockenfeller on 25. Audi motorsport chief Wolfgang Ullrich had taken the Brands Hatch result as a sign that the team was closing the gap, while Rockenfeller had been more careful, saying that a third place in Austria would tell him more than one at a circuit as different from Hockenheim and the Lausitzring as Brands Hatch was.

BMW, for its part, had two weeks to digest a second place for Spengler and a fourth for Tomczyk, and Jens Marquardt was hoping the team would be as quick in Austria as it had been in Britain. The field was the same 22 cars, eight Audis, eight Mercedes and six BMWs, to run over 47 laps.

chapters.title: Mortara takes a surprise first pole
text: Edoardo Mortara of Audi Sport Team Rosberg was quickest in qualifying with a 1:26.171, in a result that few had expected. It was his first pole position in the DTM. Paffett was second for HWA Mercedes, 0.121 seconds behind, and Ekström completed the front two rows for Audi with the third time, 0.148 seconds off, ahead of defending champion Tomczyk in the RMG BMW, who was 0.237 seconds off the pole time.

Mortara said afterwards that the car had been a real pleasure to drive. Ekström was less pleased with himself, saying that he had made a mistake on his last lap, and the Abt team director Hans-Jürgen Abt felt the team's extra lap on its tyres had told on the time. Behind the four who reached the final session, Joey Hand was fifth for BMW and Spengler sixth, with Green seventh, Mortara's team-mate Filipe Albuquerque eighth, Dirk Werner ninth and Ralf Schumacher tenth.

Augusto Farfus was 11th for BMW and Miguel Molina 12th, while Rockenfeller managed only 13th and did not reach the third session, with Christian Vietoris 14th. Adrien Tambay was 15th, Timo Scheider only 16th, and Rahel Frey 21st. David Coulthard, with 1:27.117, was last in 22nd place.

chapters.title: A pile-up on lap one and the safety car
text: Mortara did not get the best of starts and Paffett came alongside, but the Audi still reached the first corner as the leader. Ekström, who had made a good start from third, lost several places in the hectic first lap.

Behind them, the opening lap brought a series of collisions. Tambay was forced onto the grass and out of the race, and Vietoris also failed to complete the lap, while Priaulx and Werner, whose BMWs were damaged, limped to the pits and parked after one lap each. Spengler was caught between two rivals, and the damage to the front of his car cost him aerodynamic grip. The safety car came out while the cars were cleared.

chapters.title: The leaders bunch up after the second stops
text: After the restart Mortara controlled the pace at the front. Spengler continued with his damaged BMW, losing positions, and stopped for good on lap 33. Tomczyk, meanwhile, worked his way forward from fourth on the grid, and the team's practised pit stops and strategy took him up to second place.

The decisive moment came at the second stops. Mortara rejoined only just ahead of Paffett, who tried to go round the outside of the first corner after the pit exit but was pushed onto the grass, and complained about the amount of grass he had picked up. Tomczyk was soon in the fight as well. Lower down, Scheider recovered from 16th on the grid to sixth and set the fastest lap, a 1:27.027 on lap 26.

chapters.title: Mortara wins by 1.068 seconds
text: Mortara kept his composure through both attacks and crossed the line after 47 laps in 1:12:30.277, 1.068 seconds ahead of Tomczyk. Paffett was third, 2.142 seconds from the winner, and Ekström closed up in the last stages to finish fourth, 2.769 seconds behind. Green was fifth at 5.406 seconds, the last driver within half a minute of the winner.

Scheider came home sixth, more than 35 seconds behind, ahead of Rockenfeller, who moved from 13th to seventh. Albuquerque was eighth, Hand ninth and Farfus tenth, the last of the points places. Schumacher, Roberto Merhi, Robert Wickens, Susie Wolff and Frey completed the field on the lead lap. Spengler, Coulthard and Molina had retired after 33, 22 and 17 laps respectively.

chapters.title: Paffett extends the lead as Audi finally wins
text: The win was Mortara's first in the DTM, in only his 14th race, and the first for Audi in 2012. He said that his first pole one day and first win the next made him simply super-happy. Ullrich called it first-class advertisement for the DTM and for the Red Bull Ring, and said the A5 had been the measure of all things there. Five Audis finished in the top eight: Mortara, Ekström, Scheider, Rockenfeller and Albuquerque. Ekström, fourth after losing places on lap one, found it a little disappointing to miss the podium but pointed to second in the standings and a competitive car, while the Phoenix team was pleased to see Rockenfeller advance from 13th to seventh.

Paffett's third place was his fourth podium in four races and extended his lead in the standings to 83 points, 36 ahead of Ekström, who moved up to second on 47. Green was third on 44, one point ahead of Spengler, who dropped from second to fourth after his retirement. Tomczyk's second place took him to fifth on 36, with Rockenfeller sixth on 31.

BMW had mixed feelings. Tomczyk said the pit stops had been perfect and that with a little luck he could have won, and the RMG team principal Stefan Reinhold said the crew had practised stops during the week. Hand finished ninth and Farfus tenth, although Farfus's team had a problem with its equipment at his second stop. Spengler said he had been hit hard at the second corner and pushed into another car, which meant he could not attack, while Schnitzer team principal Charly Lamm said that both of his drivers lost their chances on the first lap.

The next round was the Norisring on Sunday 1 July, four weeks later, the first long break of the season. Marquardt said the BMW teams would use it to recover, while Mortara said that Rosberg had learned a lot at Spielberg and made a major step forward.

facts.v: Mortara won the 47-lap race from pole with a 1.068-second margin over Tomczyk's BMW, after fending off Paffett and Tomczyk following the second stops.
